title: Choose the visual world for shiru.sh
question: The roll assigned The Press Proof. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Press Proof
options.lineage: printer's galley and page proofs, signed off before the press run
options.thesis: Every page ships twice: the galley agents read and the finished page people read.
options.viewport: One proof sheet on the press bed: the headline set as the finished page inside trim marks, a slug line carrying the nav, and a Page proof / Galley switch that re-sets the whole sheet as Markdown.
options.risk: Turns into print nostalgia if the marks decorate instead of carrying nav, state and structure.

raised.raise: One control re-sets the entire sheet between page and galley, not a framed demo in the middle of a template.
Nothing is boxed: no cards, structure comes only from trim marks, gutters and the color bar.
State is ink registration: idle plates sit a hair out of register and the active one snaps into register.
Each section prints on its own process plate (C, M, Y, K), so the scroll reads like a set of separations.
The open-book mark is redrawn to hold at favicon and sign-off-stamp size.

options.label: The Manual Page
options.lineage: Unix man pages, one troff source typeset for print and formatted for the terminal
options.thesis: Shiru is man(1) for the web: one source, typeset for people, formatted for machines.
options.viewport: A typeset man page header (SHIRU(1)) with NAME, SYNOPSIS and DESCRIPTION, the waitlist as a SYNOPSIS line you complete.
options.risk: Familiar developer-mono territory; sits close to what dev-tool sites already do.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.lineage: green-phosphor terminals in a machine room
options.thesis: The landing page as one live transcript an agent and a person both read.
options.viewport: A transcript that curls llms.txt and prints the reply, with the waitlist as a typed prompt.
options.case: Holds audience identification (developers live in terminals); loses product clarity because the human reader half disappears.
options.risk: Near-black with one neon accent is the most common AI look for dev tools.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One pull turns a flat plane into a shaped volume.
options.viewport: A black semicircle that gathers on one control.
options.case: Fuses poorly: neither audience nor product reads in cloth.
options.kept: One control transforms the whole page.
options.risk: Fashion costume on a developer tool.

options.label: Cracktro Queue
options.thesis: Rank is depth on a black void, never a box.
options.viewport: One still line of text over drifting layers.
options.case: Fuses poorly: reads as nostalgia, hides the two-readers mechanism.
options.kept: Nothing enclosed by a rule or a box.

options.label: Movida Magazine
options.thesis: Cover lines thrown across a hard-cropped portrait.
options.viewport: A scattered cover with angled cover lines.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no grid fights documentation's job.

options.label: Sleeping City Fold
options.thesis: Districts fold into a quilt and dream their own weather.
options.viewport: A night map folding over a park.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no tie to developers or docs.
options.kept: Each region tinted its own hue.

options.label: Skate Deck Wall
options.thesis: Browse by walking a wall of full-bleed boards.
options.viewport: A rack of tall decks you pull and flip.
options.case: Fuses poorly: retail browsing, not reading.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer-docs landing page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, waitlist field, a docs screenshot, then features and FAQ.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Mintlify and its neighbours by design.
